data.answer: Yes—if it is not renewed. A registered trade mark has an initial 10-year protection period and must be renewed every 10 years to remain registered.[1] There is no fixed maximum lifespan: it can be renewed indefinitely, with the 2023 report specifying “so long as they are in use”.[2]

citations.quote: Registering a trade mark insulates it from copying and infringement for an initial period of 10 years
To remain registered, a registered trade mark must be renewed every 10 years.

claims.text: A registered trade mark has an initial 10-year protection period and must be renewed every 10 years to remain registered; it expires if not renewed.

citations.quote: Trade marks can be renewed every 10 years in perpetuity so long as they are in use

claims.text: There is no fixed maximum lifespan: a trade mark can be renewed indefinitely, with the 2023 report specifying that it must be in use.
